sources.title: Greenhouse gas removals: independent review

facts.source_fact: The government response to the independent review of greenhouse-gas removals was published on 17 July 2026.
facts.expected_handling: Attach publication date to policy-response claims.

facts.source_fact: The independent GGR review was commissioned in February 2025 to consider engineered and nature-based removals for UK net zero.
facts.expected_handling: Preserve review remit and commissioning context.

facts.source_fact: The final independent review presented 30 wide-ranging recommendations to government.
facts.expected_handling: Do not represent the government response as automatic acceptance of every recommendation.

facts.source_fact: Government strategy includes kickstarting UK GGR supply through revenue certainty via the GGR Business Model.
facts.expected_handling: Treat business-model support as policy design, not measured removals.

facts.source_fact: The strategy links GGR development with investment in carbon-capture-and-storage networks.
facts.expected_handling: Keep infrastructure policy separate from credited removal volumes.

facts.source_fact: Government aims to build durable demand through robust market frameworks.
facts.expected_handling: Treat market-demand policy as distinct from removal verification.

facts.source_fact: The response emphasises continually strengthening high-integrity standards for removals.
facts.expected_handling: Require integrity-standard provenance for credited removal claims.

facts.source_fact: GGRs are presented as important for counterbalancing residual hard-to-abate emissions on the path to net zero.
facts.expected_handling: Keep residual-emissions role separate from gross emissions reductions.

facts.source_fact: The government response does not position removals as a substitute for reducing greenhouse-gas emissions.
facts.expected_handling: Do not net removals against emissions without the applicable accounting framework.

facts.source_fact: Government has committed up to £21.7 billion over 25 years for carbon capture and storage-related support described in the response.
facts.expected_handling: Treat funding as policy context, not removal quantity.

facts.source_fact: The response references decarbonisation-readiness requirements affecting relevant energy-from-waste projects from 28 February 2026.
facts.expected_handling: Keep permitting-readiness evidence separate from achieved removals.

facts.source_fact: The response notes SAF Mandate certificate design can incentivise greenhouse-gas savings including relevant CCUS pathways.
facts.expected_handling: Require SAF scheme methodology before attributing certificate effects.

facts.source_fact: Government aims to integrate GGRs into the UK ETS as soon as practicable under appropriate rules.
facts.expected_handling: Do not treat GGRs as already fully fungible UK ETS allowances before implementation.

facts.source_fact: The response includes work to build high-integrity corporate demand for removals.
facts.expected_handling: Keep voluntary/corporate demand separate from regulatory compliance markets.

facts.source_fact: Government is developing a UK GGR Standard to support integrity and verifiability of removals.
facts.expected_handling: Require standard-version provenance when it becomes applicable.

facts.source_fact: The response references alignment with international integrity frameworks including EU CRCF, ICVCM and Article 6.4 developments.
facts.expected_handling: Do not assume equivalence between frameworks without explicit mapping.

facts.source_fact: Government agrees with the need for regulated monitoring, reporting and verification across GGR technologies.
facts.expected_handling: Require technology-appropriate MRV before verified-removal status.

facts.source_fact: Work includes development of a BSI methodology relevant to biochar greenhouse-gas removals.
facts.expected_handling: Treat methodology development as pending until the applicable method is final.

facts.source_fact: The response identifies £80 million of research and innovation investment associated with GGR development.
facts.expected_handling: Treat R&I funding as policy context rather than removal delivery evidence.

facts.source_fact: Government intends to continue monitoring public understanding and acceptance of greenhouse-gas removals.
facts.expected_handling: Keep public-attitude evidence separate from technical MRV and removal quantities.

guard_patterns.handling: Preserve government-response wording and implementation status.
guard_patterns.risk_prevented: Prevents treating proposals as completed policy.

guard_patterns.handling: Attach GGR technology, market, accounting and policy boundary.
guard_patterns.risk_prevented: Prevents mixing removals, avoided emissions and gross reductions.

guard_patterns.handling: Attach response date and implemented-versus-planned status.
guard_patterns.risk_prevented: Prevents premature use of future GGR rules.

guard_patterns.handling: Carry MRV, integrity-standard and methodology provenance.
Do not convert national GGR policy into parcel-level measured removals or emissions.
